"Xia Ziwei..." Consort Ling mused for a moment. "That girl does have exceptional qualities. It is natural for the Emperor to appreciate her. But her identity is special; we must protect her carefully and not let her become too conspicuous."

Lamei nodded. "This servant understands."

Consort Ling looked out at the deep night sky, her eyes filled with complexity. In this inner palace, who wasn't walking on thin ice? Concubine Chen relied on imperial favor to act willfully, not knowing that imperial favor was the most unreliable thing of all.

As for her, she had long ago learned to endure and wait.

Kunning Palace.

After hearing Rong Mo's report, the Empress sneered, "Concubine Chen is lifting a rock only to drop it on her own feet. The more jealous she is, the more the Emperor will be annoyed by her. Just wait and see, she will have a hard time ahead."

"Your Ladyship is wise," Rong Mo said. "But that palace maid, Xia..."

"She is just a palace maid; she cannot stir up any waves," the Empress said indifferently. "It is Consort Ling who is using the Huanzhu Princess and that maid to curry favor with the Emperor. I want to see how long she can remain smug."

She smoothed the pearl flower at her temple, a flash of cruelty in her eyes.

The night deepened, and the lights in each palace were extinguished one by one.

In Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao slept soundly in Qianlong’s arms, a satisfied smile on her lips.

chapters.title: Speak! Who Exactly Are You?
chapters.content:
What a Consort Ling! What deep, calculating schemes!

"Your Ladyship," Rong Mo whispered, "should we..."

The Empress raised a hand to stop her. She took a deep breath, forcing herself to stay calm.

This matter was of great importance and could not be handled rashly. If Xia Ziwei truly was the daughter of Xia Yuhe, then she was of royal blood and could not be touched. But if she was not...

"Go, summon Xia Ziwei to me," the Empress said in a low voice. "Tell her... I want to ask about the Huanzhu Princess's daily life."

She wanted to personally probe exactly what kind of person this girl was.

At the Shufang Studio, Ziwei was helping Little Swallow practice calligraphy. Both were startled to hear the Empress had summoned her.

"Why is the Empress looking for you?" Little Swallow was uneasy.

Ziwei suppressed the panic in her heart and said gently, "Perhaps she wants to ask about the Princess's daily routine. This servant will go and return shortly."

She followed the eunuch to Kunning Palace, her heart pounding like a drum the entire way. Why would the Empress suddenly summon a palace maid? Could it be... had she discovered something?

Inside the Kunning Palace, the Empress sat on the high seat, with Rong Mo standing to the side. The atmosphere was solemn.

Ziwei bowed according to etiquette. "This servant, Xia Ziwei, pays respects to the Empress."

The Empress did not tell her to rise, merely observing her coldly. This girl was indeed beautiful, with delicate features and a gentle temperament. Even in palace maid attire, she could not hide her scholarly air.

"Rise," the Empress said slowly. "I have heard that you serve the Huanzhu Princess very diligently."

"It is this servant's duty," Ziwei said, lowering her head.

"Before you entered the palace, was it the Fu family who sent you?" the Empress asked casually.

Ziwei’s heart tightened. "Yes. This servant was separated from my family and was fortunate to be saved by Young Master Fu, so I stayed at the Fu residence temporarily. Later, when Consort Ling needed help, she brought me into the palace."

"Oh?" The Empress raised an eyebrow. "Fu Erkang saved you? Where did he save you?"

"Near... near the Temple of Heaven," Ziwei answered carefully. "There were many people that day, and this servant was pushed down."

The Empress nodded, asking as if inadvertently, "Since you are from Jinan, have you ever heard of... Xia Yuhe?"

The words struck like a thunderclap. Ziwei trembled, her fingertips turning cold instantly. She forced herself to remain calm. "This servant... has never heard of her."

"Is that so?" The Empress stared at her. "Xia Yuhe was quite famous in Jinan back then. Since you are from Jinan, how could you have never heard of her?"

Ziwei broke into a cold sweat: "Your servant... your servant is of humble origin and has never paid attention to such things."

The Empress stopped questioning her and instead said, "I have also heard that you play chess well and write good poetry. For a palace maid, such talent is rare."

"Your servant only knows a little bit," Ziwei said, her voice trembling.

"A little bit?" the Empress suddenly snapped. "To be able to play chess with the Emperor until late at night, and to earn his personal praise—you call this 'a little bit'?!"

Ziwei fell to her knees with a thud: "Your servant... your servant was just lucky..."

"Lucky?" The Empress stood up and walked down the steps, one step at a time. "Xia Ziwei, do you take me for a fool? You carry the surname Xia, you come from Jinan, you are talented, your speech is refined, and even your tone of voice is exactly like Xia Yuhe's—tell me the truth, who exactly are you?!"

Just then, Consort Ling hurried in. Her expression was grave. As soon as she entered, she dismissed the attendants and lowered her voice: "Xiaoyanzi, was Ziwei taken away by the Empress?"

Xiaoyanzi, as if seeing a savior, nodded repeatedly: "Consort Ling, please, think of something! Ziwei has been gone for two hours and still hasn't returned!"

Consort Ling gripped her handkerchief tightly. "The Empress taking Ziwei there must mean... she has become suspicious."

Xiaoyanzi’s face turned deathly pale: "Then... will Ziwei be in danger?"

"I must find a way," Consort Ling mused. "Xiaoyanzi, don't say anything yet. I will go and beg to see the Emperor."

"But the Emperor left the palace today and won't be back until tonight!" Xiaoyanzi said anxiously.

Consort Ling’s heart sank. By the time the Emperor returned, she feared... it would be too late.

chapters.title: A Night Visit to the Jingren Palace
chapters.content:
In the Yongshou Palace, the candlelight flickered.

The Qianlong Emperor was reviewing memorials, his brows furrowed. A report on military provisions for the Northwest had just been submitted, and funds were needed for the aftermath of the floods in Jiangnan; the reports from the Ministry of Revenue crying poverty were piled half a foot high. Irritated, he set down his vermilion brush and rubbed his temples.

A pair of slender hands pressed onto his temples at the perfect moment, the pressure gentle and soft.

"Is the Emperor having a headache again?" Jiang Rao’s voice sounded by his ear, filled with concern.

Qianlong closed his eyes, letting her massage him: "These officials, all they know is how to ask for money, yet they can't come up with any solutions."

"The Emperor is a wise monarch and will surely have his own judgment," Jiang Rao said softly. "Rest for a while first. I have had rock sugar and snow pear stewed; it is the best for soothing the lungs and clearing the mind."

She turned to fetch the stewing pot, her moon-white qipao glowing softly in the candlelight. Qianlong watched her graceful back, and the irritation in his heart gradually dissipated.

Jiang Rao placed the pot on the desk and lifted the lid, letting the sweet, clear aroma fill the air. She scooped a spoonful, blew on it gently to cool it, and held it to Qianlong’s lips: "Your Majesty, have a taste."

Qianlong drank from her hand; it was sweet but not cloying, warm and smooth.

"How is it?" Jiang Rao watched him expectantly.

"Good." Qianlong nodded and pulled her to sit beside him. "You are always the most thoughtful."

Red sleeves adding fragrance, the passing of time felt peaceful.

In the Yongshou Palace, Qianlong was preparing to retire for the night. Suddenly, Wu Shulai’s voice came from outside: "Your Majesty, the Fifth Prince and the two young masters of the Fu family request an audience, saying it is an urgent matter."

Qianlong was startled: "At this late hour, what is the matter?"

Jiang Rao’s eyes flickered, and she said softly: "Perhaps there is an urgent matter from the imperial court. The Emperor should see them."

Qianlong nodded and draped his outer robe back on: "Let them in."

Yongqi and the others entered the hall. Seeing that Jiang Rao was also there, they were all taken aback, then bowed.

"Rise," Qianlong said as he sat down. "What is so urgent?"

Yongqi took a deep breath and knelt: "Imperial Father, your son... your son has come to plead for mercy."

"Plead for mercy?" Qianlong raised an eyebrow. "For whom?"

"For the Shufang Studio maid, Xia Ziwei," Yongqi said. "She does not know what wrong she has committed, but she has been locked in the Jingren Palace by the Empress. That place is cold and damp, and she is but a weak woman..."

Qianlong frowned: "The Empress has her reasons for detaining a palace maid. How do you know that the maid is innocent?"

"Imperial Father," Xiaoyanzi also knelt, her eyes brimming with tears, "Ziwei really didn't do anything wrong! She spends every day helping me read and write, and she is very well-behaved... Imperial Father, didn't you also praise her for her talent? Please, save her..."

Qianlong looked at Xiaoyanzi’s tear-reddened eyes and his heart softened, but he still said, "The Empress has her own judgment regarding matters of the inner palace. It is not appropriate for me to intervene."

"Your Majesty," Fu Erkang suddenly spoke up, "Miss Xia... once spoke to me of her background. Her mother passed away early, leaving her alone and helpless. She traveled thousands of miles to the capital to find her relatives, only to become separated from them. Such an experience is already pitiful enough. If she were to suffer an unjust accusation..."

He spoke subtly, but it stirred something in Qianlong’s heart. Searching for relatives... an orphan girl...

For some reason, he recalled the expression on Ziwei’s face when she mentioned her mother that day, and that phrase, "A woman should also be well-read and reasonable..."

"Enough." Qianlong stood up. "I will accompany you to the Jingren Palace to see. If that maid is truly innocent, I will naturally see justice done for her."

Yongqi and the others were overjoyed and thanked him repeatedly.

Qianlong said to Jiang Rao: "You rest first; I will return shortly."

Jiang Rao nodded submissively: "Your servant will wait for the Emperor."

Yongqi and Fu Erkang exchanged a glance, their eyes filled with concern.

chapters.title: The Dumpling Banquet Incident
chapters.content:
Ziwei recuperated in the Shufang Studio for half a month, and her injuries gradually healed. Qianlong sent imperial physicians to check on her daily, and rewards flowed into the Shufang Studio like water. Xiaoyanzi stayed by her side constantly, and Jin Suo took meticulous care of her.

On this day, Ziwei was finally able to walk around the courtyard. Xiaoyanzi excitedly took her hands and spun her around: "Ziwei, you’re finally better! We must celebrate!"

"How shall we celebrate?" Ziwei asked with a gentle smile.

"Make dumplings!" Xiaoyanzi’s eyes lit up. "When I was at the Great Courtyard, Liu Qing and Liu Hong said that in the North, when there is a happy occasion, people make dumplings! Let’s make a lot and let the consorts of every palace taste the craftsmanship of the Shufang Studio!"

Ziwei was startled upon hearing this: "This... this is too ostentatious. What delicacies have the consorts not tasted? Why bother..."

"Oh, you are too cautious!" Xiaoyanzi patted her chest. "Imperial Father said he would compensate you well, so let’s have a lively celebration! Mingyue! Caixia! Go to the Imperial Kitchen and get the best flour and fillings!"

The news quickly spread throughout the six palaces.

In the Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao was grinding ink for Qianlong.

Upon hearing the report from Suxin that the Shufang Studio was holding a dumpling banquet and intended to send dumplings to every palace, Jiang Rao’s hand paused slightly.

It was happening... In the original story, this dumpling banquet was the farce that caused everyone in the palace to suffer from diarrhea. She remembered clearly that it was the Empress who instructed Nanny Rong to put croton powder into the fillings.

"Your Majesty, the Shufang Studio is holding a dumpling banquet," Jiang Rao said, keeping her expression calm as she continued to grind the ink. "The Princess Pearl is truly thoughtful, wanting everyone in the palaces to have a taste."

Qianlong looked up from his memorials and laughed: "That Xiaoyanzi, she only knows how to stir things up. But since the girl Ziwei has recovered, a little liveliness is fine."

Jiang Rao sighed inwardly. Although this farce in the original plot was humiliating, it was an important turning point that pushed the story forward; the Empress lost further favor because of it, and Qianlong became even more sympathetic toward the Shufang Studio.

"Your Majesty," Jiang Rao said softly, "My stomach has been a bit uncomfortable these past few days, and the physician said I need a light diet. If the Princess sends dumplings over, I fear I won't have the fortune to enjoy them."

Qianlong looked at her with concern: "Why didn't you say so earlier? Have you seen a physician?"

"I have. They said it's a common minor ailment during the change of seasons and that a few doses of medicine will fix it," Jiang Rao smiled gently. "It is just a pity, as I hear Miss Xia’s craftsmanship is excellent."

In the Kunning Palace, the Empress had been confined for reflection for half a month.

Hearing that the Shufang Studio was holding a dumpling banquet and intended to send them to all the palaces, the brush the Empress was using to copy Buddhist scriptures stopped abruptly, and the ink bled into a stain on the rice paper.

"A fine Xia Ziwei, acting so brazenly as soon as she recovers," the Empress sneered. "I want to see just how long you can remain triumphant."

Although Nanny Rong had been dismissed, she still had her ways. She slipped into the palace and whispered: "Your Majesty, this is an opportunity... There is a young eunuch in the Imperial Kitchen whose brother works in the pharmacy..."

The Empress was silent for a long time before slowly saying: "Do it cleanly."

The Shufang Studio was bustling with activity.

Xiaoyanzi kneaded the dough herself, Ziwei wrapped the dumplings, and Yongqi, Erkang, and Ertai all came to help. Once baskets of dumplings were wrapped, Xiaoyanzi ordered happily: "Quick, quick, send them to the palaces while they’re hot! And it’s settled—everyone is eating dumplings for dinner tonight!"

When the dumplings were delivered to the Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao was accompanying Qianlong for dinner.

"Your Majesty, the dumplings from the Shufang Studio have arrived," Wu Shulai reported.

Qianlong laughed: "Bring them up. Rao’er, will you have a taste?"

Jiang Rao looked at the steaming plate of dumplings, and alarm bells rang in her heart. However, she smiled gently: "Your Majesty, please eat first. I just took my medicine, and the physician instructed me to have an empty stomach for half an hour."

She had carefully calculated the time—in the original story, the diarrhea struck around midnight. It was just after dusk, so her excuse of dietary restrictions due to medicine was perfectly reasonable.

Qianlong did not suspect anything and picked up a dumpling to taste: "Hmm, the taste is not bad. That girl Ziwei truly has a pair of skillful hands."

Jiang Rao served him dishes, but she did not touch a single one herself. She watched Qianlong eat three or four dumplings, feeling anxious inside but unable to speak the truth.

"Your Majesty, don't just eat dumplings; have some soup." She served him a bowl of clear soup, hoping to dilute the effect of the poison.

At midnight, the storm broke.

In his sleep, Qianlong was suddenly struck by agonizing abdominal pain and sat up abruptly.

"Wu Shulai!" He clutched his stomach, his face deathly pale.

Wu Shulai, who was on night duty outside, scrambled in: "Your Majesty! What is wrong?"

"Quick... call the imperial physician..." Qianlong was in such pain that cold sweat poured down his face.

Almost simultaneously, sounds of panic erupted from every palace. Consort Ling’s Yanxi Palace, Consort Qing’s Chuxiu Palace, Concubine Wan’s Zhongcui Palace... the consorts were all suffering from varying degrees of diarrhea and abdominal pain, and the entire inner palace was in chaos.

In the Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao "timely" woke up.

Hearing the commotion from Qianlong, she hurriedly threw on a robe and got up: "Your Majesty, what is wrong?"

"Abdominal pain..." Qianlong was in too much pain to speak.

Jiang Rao understood the situation, but she put on a look of panic: "How could you suddenly have abdominal pain? You were fine at dinner... could it be..." She deliberately trailed off.

"The dumplings..." Qianlong also realized, "Every palace ate the dumplings today..."

Jiang Rao hurriedly called for help: "Quick, summon the imperial physician! And seal up the remaining dumplings from dinner!"

The imperial physician rushed over, and after checking the pulse, his expression was grave: "Your Majesty has been poisoned... it appears to be caused by a laxative like croton."

Qianlong’s face turned livid: "Investigate! Investigate this thoroughly for me!"

The Imperial Medical Academy held a consultation, and the truth came to light.

All the consorts suffering from diarrhea had the same symptoms, all having eaten the dumplings sent by the Shufang Studio. The Imperial Kitchen was sealed and interrogated overnight, and the young eunuch, unable to withstand the torture, confessed about Nanny Rong.

"Rong Mo said... said it was to teach Xia Ziwei a lesson... to let her know that the palace is not a place where she can be arrogant..." the young eunuch confessed, crying and wailing.

Qianlong was furious: "What a poisonous woman! Throw her into the dungeon and interrogate her with torture! To think that while the Empress was confined to her quarters, she still instigated a wicked servant to commit such evil; extend her confinement to three months! Dock her salary for half a year!"

When the decree reached the Kunming Palace, the Empress smashed her favorite enamel vase.

"Useless! All of you are useless!" She trembled with rage, "You couldn't even handle such a small matter!"

Inside the Yongshou Palace, Qianlong lay on his bed, exhausted.

Jiang Rao personally fed him his medicine, her eyes filled with heartache: "Your Majesty has suffered."

Qianlong held her hand: "Fortunately, you didn't eat... otherwise you would have suffered this ordeal too."

Jiang Rao sighed inwardly. She wasn't lucky; she knew the plot. But she couldn't say that, so she only said softly: "Your concubine happened to be avoiding certain foods while taking medicine, so I dodged a bullet. It’s just that Your Majesty..."

As she spoke, her eyes turned slightly red: "That Rong Mo is too vicious; this was meant to harm the Imperial body!"

Qianlong felt a warmth in his heart and pulled her into his arms: "With you by my side, I feel at ease."

Inside the Shufang Studio, Xiaoyanzi was crying her eyes out.

"I really didn't know the dumplings were problematic... I just wanted to make everyone happy..." she sobbed, breathless.

Ziwei comforted her softly: "It’s not your fault; someone harmed us on purpose."

Erkang said in a deep voice: "This was aimed at the Shufang Studio. Although Rong Mo was caught, the Empress will not let it rest."

Yongqi nodded: "We must be more careful with our food from now on."

Jiang Rao sat alone by the window, looking at the night sky.

This storm had finally passed. She had successfully avoided the disaster of diarrhea and protected Qianlong—though she couldn't stop it entirely, at least she made him eat fewer dumplings, and his symptoms were milder.

"Your Highness, it's late, please rest," the maid reminded her softly.

Jiang Rao nodded, but thought to herself: This world of *My Fair Princess* is truly bustling with activity.

chapters.title: Then Go Find Yourself a Dignified Concubine!
chapters.content:
Only seven days had passed since the dumpling banquet farce, and in the Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao was throwing a tantrum in front of the mirror.

"Is there no way to live anymore!" She swept the rouge and powder off the vanity onto the floor, "Every day it’s either learning etiquette or copying Buddhist scriptures! I entered the palace to enjoy life, not to become a nun!"

Suxin hurriedly squatted down to clean up: "Your Highness, please calm your anger. The Empress Dowager is returning to the palace, and all six palaces are preparing..."

"Preparing for what? Preparing to be scolded?" Jiang Rao sat on the couch, fuming, "During the last dumpling banquet, the Empress played dirty and poisoned the food, causing the whole palace to have diarrhea. Now that the Empress Dowager is coming back, who knows what she’ll think of us! I think she’s just here to clean up the mess!"

The more she thought about it, the angrier she got: "It’s all because of that Xiaoyanzi, why did she have to make dumplings! If she had to make them, why did she have to send them to every palace! Now it’s a disaster, the whole palace is poisoned, the Emperor had diarrhea for three days, and I had to worry along with him—even though I was smart enough not to eat, I still had to serve him while he was sick!"

Suxin couldn't help but laugh: "Didn't Your Highness say at the time that it was 'a perfect way to lose weight'?"

"I was just saying that out of anger!" Jiang Rao glared at her, "The Emperor was sick, didn't I have to serve him tea and water? Didn't I have to stay up all night watching over him? Look at these dark circles under my eyes, they haven't faded yet!"

Just as she was speaking, Qianlong's voice came from outside: "Who made my Consort Chen stay up all night?"

Seeing Qianlong enter, Jiang Rao didn't get up and turned her face away: "Who else could it be? Your Majesty yourself! You were greedy at the dumpling banquet, ate so many, who can you blame for the diarrhea?"

Qianlong was left speechless by her retort and sat down beside her: "I was unaware of the situation."

Qianlong smiled and pulled her into his arms, "This time it's thanks to you not eating, otherwise, if I were sick, who would take care of me?"

"Hmph, now you know your concubine's worth?" Jiang Rao remained unforgiving, "Then why does Your Majesty force me to learn etiquette? With the Empress Dowager returning, even if I learn my etiquette well, can I compare to the Empress? Can I compare to Consort Ling? One played dirty and poisoned the food, the other failed to discipline—disciplining a Xiaoyanzi and causing a dumpling banquet! If you want to blame someone, blame them!"

Qianlong was stunned by her twisted logic, then laughed: "You, you always have your reasons."

"It's true!" Jiang Rao struggled out of his arms, "Your Majesty, think about it, who organized the dumpling banquet? Xiaoyanzi. Who taught Xiaoyanzi? Consort Ling. Who touched the dumpling filling? Rong Mo. Whose person is Rong Mo? The Empress. Following this chain, what does it have to do with me? I was staying quietly in the Yongshou Palace, why should I have to learn etiquette?"

The more she spoke, the more she felt she was right: "If the Empress Dowager wants to blame someone, she should blame them! But Your Majesty, instead of punishing them, you punish me—making me study the *Women's Precepts* and *Women's Lessons*, I get a headache just looking at them!"

Qianlong was left with no temper by her unreasonable pestering and had to coax her: "Alright, alright, you don't have to study them. But on the day the Empress Dowager returns, you must at least..."

"Your concubine knows!" Jiang Rao interrupted, "Bow and pay respects, I can do that! But Your Majesty must promise me that if the Empress Dowager gets angry because of the dumpling banquet, you must say it was the Empress and Consort Ling's fault, and you cannot implicate me!"

"Why would the Empress Dowager be angry for no reason?" Qianlong chuckled.

"That's not for certain," Jiang Rao said seriously, "The dumpling banquet scandal is known throughout the palace; can the Empress Dowager not know? If she knows, can she not be angry? If she's angry, won't she need someone to vent on? Your Majesty, promise me first, if she wants to vent, go find the Empress and Consort Ling, don't come looking for me!"

Qianlong was left with no choice but to nod: "Alright, alright, I promise you."

In the Shufang Studio, Xiaoyanzi was crying to Consort Ling.

"Consort Ling, I really didn't mean it..." her eyes were as swollen as walnuts, "I just wanted to make everyone happy, who knew the dumplings were problematic..."

Consort Ling sighed: "I know you didn't mean it. But the Empress Dowager is returning, and if this reaches her ears, I'm afraid she will be displeased."

"Then what should I do?" Xiaoyanzi panicked, "Will the Empress Dowager kick me out of the palace?"

Ziwei comforted her from the side: "Princess, don't be afraid, the Emperor loves you so much, he won't let the Empress Dowager kick you out."

"But..." Xiaoyanzi's tears fell again, "What if the Empress Dowager doesn't like me? I caused the dumpling banquet, and the whole palace had diarrhea... The Empress Dowager must think I'm a disaster..."

Consort Ling said softly: "That's why you must learn your etiquette well. If the Empress Dowager sees you are well-behaved and sensible, perhaps she won't hold it against you."

Xiaoyanzi made a bitter face: "But I can't learn it... those rules are too hard..."

"You must learn even if you can't," Consort Ling said, unusually stern, "The Empress Dowager values etiquette above all else. If you lose your composure in front of her, even the Emperor won't be able to protect you."

Xiaoyanzi shivered in fear and finally began to study diligently.

In the Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao was picking out a gift for the Empress Dowager's return.

"This jade Guanyin is nice," she picked up a Guanyin statue carved from mutton-fat white jade, "The material is good, and the carving is excellent. Suxin, wrap it up."

"Your Highness," Suxin reminded her, "The Empress Dowager worships Buddha, so a Guanyin statue is good, but wouldn't it be too expensive? The other concubines are sending..."

"They send what they send, I send what I send," Jiang Rao said nonchalantly, "The Empress is confined to her quarters and can't send anything good. Consort Ling is busy worrying about Xiaoyanzi and has no time to prepare anything carefully. If I send a generous gift now, the Empress Dowager will know who is thoughtful."

She paused and added: "Besides, the Empress Dowager must be unhappy about the dumpling banquet. I'll send a generous gift to make her happy."

Suxin smiled: "Your Highness is very thoughtful."

"That goes without saying," Jiang Rao said proudly.

As she spoke, her mood improved, and she even found the jewelry and ornaments pleasing to the eye: "By the way, where is the new dress I ordered? On the day the Empress Dowager returns, I must look beautiful."

"It's still at the embroidery workshop," Suxin said, "The Xiaying gauze material you wanted is rare, and the embroiderers are working day and night, saying they need to embroider for a full eighty-one hours."

"Urge them," Jiang Rao said, "I must try it on before the Empress Dowager returns."

Days passed, and the day of the Empress Dowager's return arrived.

Early that morning, the concubines of the six palaces gathered at the palace gate to welcome her. Jiang Rao was wearing the new rouge-colored Xiaying gauze dress, standing out in the crowd.

Consort Ling quietly pulled her sleeve: "Sister, is this outfit today... a bit too flashy?"

"Flashy?" Jiang Rao looked down, "I think it's just right. The Empress Dowager's return is a joyous occasion, what's wrong with dressing festively?"

No sooner had she finished speaking than the sound of ceremonial music began—the Empress Dowager's carriage had arrived.

Everyone knelt down. Jiang Rao secretly looked up and saw a bright yellow carriage slowly stop. A maid lifted the curtain, and a dignified and noble old woman stepped out, supported by a nanny.

It was the Empress Dowager.

"Welcome back to the palace, Empress Dowager, may you live ten thousand years!" everyone shouted in unison.

The Empress Dowager's gaze swept over the crowd, paused on Jiang Rao, and then looked at Xiaoyanzi.

"Everyone rise," the Empress Dowager's voice was calm but carried authority.

Everyone stood up. The Empress Dowager spoke a few words to Qianlong, then turned her gaze back to Jiang Rao.

"Emperor," the Empress Dowager said slowly, "Who is this in the rouge-colored dress?"

Qianlong hurriedly said: "Reporting to Imperial Mother, this is Consort Chen of the Jiang clan."

The Empress Dowager nodded and said faintly: "The dress is nice. But to dress so flashily while welcoming the carriage today seems a bit frivolous."

Jiang Rao's face turned pale.

Xiaoyanzi was suddenly delighted.

Qianlong hurriedly smoothed things over: "Imperial Mother, Consort Chen is young and doesn't know any better..."

"Age is no excuse," the Empress Dowager interrupted him, "The concubines of the six palaces should prioritize dignity."

After saying this, she stopped looking at Jiang Rao and turned to walk toward the Cining Palace.

Everyone followed quickly. Jiang Rao stood where she was, biting her lip, her eyes gradually turning red.

Consort Ling walked past her and quietly squeezed her hand: "Sister, don't take it to heart."

Jiang Rao shook off her hand and turned to leave.

Back at the Yongshou Palace, as soon as Jiang Rao entered, she tore the hairpins from her head and threw them on the floor.

"Frivolous? She called me frivolous?" She trembled with anger, "Why is it frivolous to wear a beautiful dress? Just because she dresses in drab colors, does the whole palace have to follow suit?"

Suxin hurriedly persuaded her: "Your Highness, please calm your anger, the Empress Dowager was just speaking casually..."

"Speaking casually?" Jiang Rao sneered, "She said it in front of so many people, and you call that casual? I think she did it on purpose!"

The more she spoke, the angrier she became, sweeping all the tea sets on the table onto the floor: "Isn't she just the Empress Dowager? What's so great about that! It's enough that the Emperor likes me, who cares if she likes me!"

When Qianlong entered, he saw the mess on the floor and Jiang Rao crying on the bed.

He walked over and gently patted her back: "Rao'er..."

"Get away, Your Majesty!" Jiang Rao did not look back. "I am frivolous and unworthy of you, Your Majesty. You had better go find a more dignified consort!"

Qianlong felt his heart soften at her tears and could only coax her: "Alright, alright, stop crying. I promise you, if the Empress Dowager gives you a hard time again in the future, I will certainly protect you."

"Do you mean what you say, Your Majesty?"

"I mean it."

Jiang Rao felt slightly better, but she was still nursing a grudge. She looked up at Qianlong with red-rimmed eyes: "Then you must stay with me tonight, Your Majesty."

Qianlong smiled: "Very well, I will stay with you." He lowered his head and kissed her red, swollen lips, which were still puffy from crying...

In the Cining Palace, the Empress Dowager was listening to the nanny report on the situation in the various palaces.

"The one in Yongshou Palace went back and threw quite a tantrum; she broke quite a few things," the nanny said cautiously.

The Empress Dowager took a sip of tea and said indifferently, "She certainly has quite a temper."

"The Emperor has already gone to coax her," the nanny added.

The Empress Dowager set down her teacup: "Has the matter of the dumpling banquet been investigated clearly?"

"It has," the nanny replied. "It was Nanny Rong who instigated the young eunuch in the Imperial Kitchen to poison the food. Nanny Rong has been thrown into the celestial prison, and the Empress is confined to her quarters to reflect on her mistakes."

The Empress Dowager was silent for a moment, then said slowly, "The Empress is becoming increasingly unreasonable."

She paused, then added, "As for that Consort Chen... she was indeed dressed a bit too gaudily today. But she is young, and it is only natural for her to love dressing up."

The nanny probed, "Would the Empress Dowager like to summon..."

"No rush," the Empress Dowager waved her hand.

chapters.title: Audience at Cining Palace
chapters.content:
Jiang Rao was still sulking.

She sat before her vanity, looking at her still-red and swollen eyes in the mirror, feeling more aggrieved the more she thought about it: "Suxin, do you think the Empress Dowager finds me an eyesore? What is wrong with wearing a beautiful dress? How is that frivolous?"

As Suxin combed her hair, she gently persuaded her: "My Lady, please don't overthink it. The Empress Dowager was just speaking off the cuff..."

"Off the cuff?" Jiang Rao pouted. "Why didn't she say anything about the Empress? Or Consort Ling? She just fixated on me! I think she just feels uncomfortable because I am young and beautiful, and the Emperor favors me!"

Just as she was speaking, a young eunuch's voice came from outside: "My Lady, someone has come from the Cining Palace."

Jiang Rao was startled: "The Cining Palace? Is the Empress Dowager looking for me?"

"It is not for you, My Lady," the young eunuch said. "The Empress Dowager has summoned the Return Pearl Princess. The eunuch delivering the message just came from the Shufang Studio and passed by here."

Jiang Rao's eyes lit up: "The Empress Dowager summoned Little Swallow?"

"Yes, she said the Return Pearl Princess is to go to the Cining Palace for an audience immediately."

Jiang Rao was suddenly delighted: "Good! She laughed at me yesterday! Now it's her turn! Suxin, hurry, help me change my clothes. I want to go watch the show!"

"My Lady, this... is that appropriate?"

"What is inappropriate about it?" Jiang Rao stood up. "I'm just going to wander outside the Cining Palace, not go in. I want to see how the Empress Dowager 'instructs' our Return Pearl Princess!"

In the Shufang Studio, Little Swallow was gloating.

"Haha! Did you see that? The Empress Dowager said yesterday that Consort Chen was frivolous! Said her clothes were too gaudy!" Little Swallow laughed until she was doubled over. "I told you so, why wear so much red? Like she's about to get married!"

Ziwei said helplessly, "Princess, please don't laugh. Consort Chen is, after all, a consort..."

"So what if she's a consort? Didn't the Empress Dowager criticize her anyway?" Little Swallow said triumphantly. "I think the Empress Dowager is sensible; she knows who is good and who is bad."

No sooner had she finished speaking than an announcement came from outside: "Nanny Sun from the Cining Palace has arrived—"

Little Swallow was stunned: "The Cining Palace? Looking for me?"

Nanny Sun walked in and bowed properly: "This old servant pays respects to the Return Pearl Princess. The Empress Dowager has issued an oral decree: please come to the Cining Palace for an audience immediately, Princess."

Little Swallow's smile froze on her face: "R-right now?"

"Yes, please follow me, Princess." Nanny Sun's tone was respectful but brooked no refusal.

Little Swallow panicked and grabbed Ziwei's hand: "Ziwei, come with me!"

Ziwei was also in a difficult position: "Princess, the Empress Dowager only summoned you..."

"I don't care! You have to come with me!" Little Swallow gripped Ziwei tightly. "If you don't go, I won't go!"

Nanny Sun looked at Ziwei, pondered for a moment, and said, "Then this maid may come along as well."

Little Swallow finally breathed a sigh of relief, but her heart was still pounding. Her hands were shaking as she changed her clothes: "Ziwei, why is the Empress Dowager looking for me? Is she going to scold me?"

Ziwei helped her adjust her collar and comforted her softly: "Don't be afraid, Princess. The Empress Dowager summoned you today perhaps just to see you."

The two followed Nanny Sun toward the Cining Palace. On the way, Little Swallow saw Jiang Rao strolling in the Imperial Garden with Suxin, and her anger flared—this was clearly to watch her suffer!

Jiang Rao walked over with a smile: "Where is the Return Pearl Princess off to?"

Little Swallow said irritably: "To the Cining Palace to see the Empress Dowager!"

"Oh?" Jiang Rao feigned surprise. "Summoned by the Empress Dowager? Then you must be careful, Princess. The Empress Dowager is very strict about etiquette; be careful with your words and ensure your bows are standard, otherwise..."

She deliberately drew out her words, and Little Swallow's face turned even paler.

Ziwei quickly bowed: "Greetings, Consort Chen."

Jiang Rao waved her hand: "Hurry along, don't keep the Empress Dowager waiting."

Watching Little Swallow's flustered back, Jiang Rao was in high spirits: "Let's go, Suxin, let's go wander near the Cining Palace."

In the Cining Palace, the atmosphere was solemn.

The Empress Dowager sat upright at the head of the main hall, twisting prayer beads in her hand, her expression dignified.

Little Swallow walked into the hall, her legs turning to jelly. She knelt down properly: "G-granddaughter pays respects to the Imperial Grandmother. May the Imperial Grandmother be auspicious."

This was what Consort Ling had taught her countless times, and she finally hadn't said it wrong.

The Empress Dowager glanced at her and said indifferently, "Rise."

Little Swallow stood up tremblingly, hands at her sides, not daring to breathe.

The Empress Dowager scrutinized her for a long time before speaking: "I heard you grew up among the common people before entering the palace?"

"Yes..." Little Swallow's voice trembled.

The Empress Dowager nodded, did not pursue the matter further, and instead asked: "How is your study of etiquette coming along?"

"I am... I am learning," Little Swallow answered honestly.

"Hmm," the Empress Dowager twisted her prayer beads. "I called you here today because I wanted to see you. Since the Emperor has accepted you as his daughter, it is only natural that I accept you as my granddaughter."

Little Swallow felt a warmth in her heart, and her eyes even turned a bit red: "Th-thank you, Imperial Grandmother."

Seeing her like this, the Empress Dowager's expression softened slightly: "It is natural that you don't understand the rules, as you have just entered the palace. But you must be more careful in the future and not cause any more trouble."

"Yes..." Little Swallow quickly agreed.

The Empress Dowager then asked if she was accustomed to living in the palace and if she was adapting to the food. Although her tone was calm, it showed concern. Little Swallow answered one by one, becoming more relaxed with each answer, and by the end, she was not as afraid anymore.

After about the time it takes to drink a cup of tea, the Empress Dowager waved her hand: "That is all for today, you may go. Come to the Cining Palace to pay your respects often in the future."

Little Swallow felt as if she had been granted amnesty and quickly bowed to withdraw. As she walked out of the Cining Palace, she was still in a daze—the Empress Dowager hadn't scolded her? And she had even shown concern for her?

Outside the palace gate, Jiang Rao was "coincidentally" passing by.

Seeing Little Swallow's distracted expression, she leaned in and asked: "What's wrong? Did the Empress Dowager lecture you?"

Little Swallow shook her head and muttered: "The Empress Dowager... she didn't scold me. She even asked if I was eating well and if I was used to living here..."

Jiang Rao was stunned: "Just that?"

"Yes." Little Swallow nodded, then suddenly thought of something and looked at Jiang Rao triumphantly: "The Empress Dowager even told me to come pay my respects often!"

Jiang Rao's expression stiffened, and she snorted: "That's because she hasn't seen what you're usually like!"

"Even if she saw, she didn't say anything to me!" Little Swallow was even more smug.

Jiang Rao was so angry she turned and walked away. Suxin quickly followed: "My Lady, please calm your anger..."

"I refuse!" Jiang Rao gritted her teeth. "The Empress Dowager is biased! She spoke to me so harshly, but she was so kind and gentle to Little Swallow!"

Just then, Nanny Sun came out of the Cining Palace.

Seeing Jiang Rao, Nanny Sun came over and bowed: "Consort Chen."

Jiang Rao forced a smile: "Nanny Sun."

"The Empress Dowager has asked me to deliver a message," Nanny Sun said. "Tomorrow, all the consorts are invited to the Cining Palace to listen to the sutras. The Empress Dowager specifically said that Consort Chen must be present."

Jiang Rao's heart sank—this was aimed at her.

But she smiled on the surface: "Understood, thank you for the message, Nanny."

Once Nanny Sun had left, Jiang Rao's face fell: "Listen to sutras? Listen to what sutras? I think it's a lecture!"

Back at Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao threw herself onto the bed and cried.

When Qianlong arrived, he saw her crying like rain on pear blossoms: "Your Majesty! The Empress Dowager wants us to listen to sutras tomorrow, and she specifically had Nanny Sun tell me that I must be there! Is she going to punish me? Is it because she called me frivolous yesterday, and she wants to embarrass me in public tomorrow?"

Qianlong hurriedly coaxed her: "That won't happen. The Empress Dowager just wants everyone to listen to Buddhist teachings..."

"Then why did she specifically have Nanny Sun deliver the message?" Jiang Rao raised her teary eyes. "Why didn't she just say 'all the consorts,' but instead said 'especially Consort Chen'? If this isn't targeting me, what is it?"

Qianlong was stunned by her question.

Seeing that he didn't speak, Jiang Rao cried even harder: "You said you would protect me yesterday, Your Majesty, and today you've changed! The Empress Dowager is going to punish me, and you won't even intervene!"

"I didn't say I wouldn't protect you," Qianlong said, feeling a headache coming on. "It's just listening to sutras, what could possibly happen?"

"How could nothing happen?" Jiang Rao sobbed. "The Empress Dowager is making me go, she will definitely test me on Buddhist teachings. I don't understand those things, and if I can't answer, she will say I am unlearned and unworthy of you, Your Majesty... By then, the whole palace will be laughing at me!"

The more she spoke, the more aggrieved she felt: "I'm not going! I'll just say I'm sick and can't get out of bed!"

Qianlong could do nothing with her and had to coax her: "Alright, alright, I will go with you. I will go listen to the sutras tomorrow too. If the Empress Dowager gives you a hard time, I will speak up for you, okay?"

"Really?" Jiang Rao raised her teary eyes.

"Really." Qianlong wiped away her tears.

Jiang Rao felt a little better, but she was still anxious. She leaned into Qianlong's arms and said gloomily: "Your Majesty, does the Empress Dowager not like me?"

Qianlong held her: "How could that be? The Empress Dowager is just a bit strict."

"Then why is she so good to Little Swallow?" Jiang Rao looked up. "Little Swallow caused such a huge incident with the dumpling banquet, and the Empress Dowager didn't even scold her. I just wore a red dress, and I was called frivolous..."

Qianlong was momentarily speechless.

Seeing that he couldn't answer, Jiang Rao felt aggrieved again: "You are biased, Your Majesty! Biased toward Little Swallow, biased toward the Empress Dowager, but not toward me!"

Qianlong, finding her fussing a headache, had no choice but to coax her again: "I favor you, I favor you the most."

Jiang Rao leaned into Qianlong's arms, but her heart was still pounding. With the Empress Dowager back, she feared this would be an endless ordeal.

However, with the Emperor protecting her, she wasn't afraid.

Thinking this, her mood improved, and she reached out to wrap her arms around Qianlong's neck: "Your Majesty, dine with me tonight."

Qianlong smiled: "Very well, I will."

In the Cining Palace, the Empress Dowager was fingering her prayer beads.

Nanny Sun, who was attending to her, said softly: "Consort Chen... seems rather displeased."

The Empress Dowager said indifferently: "Young and impetuous, it is only natural."

She paused, then added: "At tomorrow's scripture reading, I shall see for myself how many of the concubines in the six palaces are truly devoted to the Buddha."

chapters.title: The Bloodline the Emperor Left in Jinan?
chapters.content:
In the Buddhist hall of the Cining Palace, sandalwood incense curled in the air.

The Empress Dowager fingered her prayer beads, eyes closed in meditation. Nanny Sun walked in on tiptoe and whispered: "Empress Dowager, the Empress has arrived."

"Let her in." The Empress Dowager opened her eyes, her gaze clear.

The Empress walked into the Buddhist hall and performed a formal salute: "This concubine pays her respects to the Empress Dowager."

"Rise, sit." The Empress Dowager gestured to the seat beside her. "During these days you spent reflecting in seclusion, you should have plenty to tell me about the affairs of the palace."

The Empress sat down cautiously and spoke after careful consideration: "During the time the Empress Dowager was away from the palace, quite a lot has indeed happened. The most pressing matter... is the entry of Princess Huanzhu into the palace."

The Empress Dowager’s expression remained unchanged: "I saw that girl yesterday. They say she is the bloodline the Emperor left in Jinan during his southern tour?"

"That is correct," the Empress said. "The Emperor says she is the daughter of Xia Yuhe, seventeen years old this year, the bloodline he left behind during his southern tour back then."

The Empress Dowager’s hand, which was fingering the beads, paused: "Xia Yuhe's daughter... is there proof?"

"There is a painting of mist and rain, and a line of poetry," the Empress recalled carefully. "The Emperor said the painting was drawn by Xia Yuhe herself, and the poem was the one they pledged their love with back then. I have seen it; it is indeed the Emperor's handwriting."

"Hmm." The Empress Dowager pondered for a moment. "What is the girl's temperament like?"

The Empress replied truthfully: "Innocent and artless, with no hidden motives, but her manners are truly lacking. Having grown up among the common folk, she does not understand palace etiquette and often makes a laughingstock of herself."

A flash of complexity crossed the Empress Dowager’s eyes: "Xia Yuhe's daughter... is like this?"

"The Empress Dowager may not know," the Empress continued, "that there is a palace maid by Princess Huanzhu's side named Xia Ziwei, who was brought into the palace by Lord Fu Lun. This girl is well-read and sensible, proficient in music, chess, calligraphy, and painting, and is highly regarded by the Emperor."

The Empress Dowager raised her eyes: "A palace maid, regarded by the Emperor?"

"Yes." The Empress weighed her words. "I also find it strange. This Xia Ziwei is also from Jinan, surnamed Xia, and is of similar age to Princess Huanzhu. The Emperor... seems to show her special concern. A few days ago, when this maid was injured, the Emperor went to the Jingren Palace himself to save her and even ordered the imperial physician to use the best medicine for her treatment."

The Empress Dowager frowned slightly: "Empress, there is more to your words than meets the ear."

The Empress hurriedly stood up and knelt: "I dare not speak recklessly. I only find it too coincidental—two women from Jinan with the surname Xia of similar age, one became a princess, the other a palace maid. And..."

She paused and lowered her voice: "And I have heard that this Xia Ziwei’s conduct and speech are quite refined, and her conversation and insight are not like those of an ordinary commoner. On the contrary, Princess Huanzhu... although lively and cute, knows nothing of poetry or literature, which does not quite match the Emperor’s description of Xia Yuhe’s exceptional talent back then."

The Empress Dowager was silent for a long time, then said slowly: "Are you suspecting... that there is a problem with Princess Huanzhu's identity?"

"I dare not!" The Empress prostrated herself. "I only find it suspicious. Moreover, Consort Ling takes special care of Xia Ziwei, and she is also the one teaching Princess Huanzhu her manners. In this..."

"Consort Ling?" A sharp glint appeared in the Empress Dowager’s eyes. "How is she doing in the palace now?"

The Empress said cautiously: "Consort Ling assists in managing the six palaces with propriety and is highly trusted by the Emperor. It is just... she is too close to the Shufang Studio and takes extra care of both Princess Huanzhu and Xia Ziwei. I always feel it is quite unusual."

The Empress Dowager allowed the Empress to rise and said slowly: "I am aware of these matters. What else?"

"There is also Consort Chen, of the Jiang clan." The Empress sat back down. "This Consort Chen entered the palace three years ago and has been deeply favored by the Emperor ever since. She is spoiled and often speaks and acts without consideration. The Emperor... grants her almost every request."

The Empress Dowager remembered the concubine in the rouge-colored dress who had greeted her yesterday and said indifferently: "I have seen her; she is indeed young and impetuous."

"The Empress Dowager is right," the Empress sighed. "For the past three years, the Emperor has almost exclusively favored Consort Chen, and there is much grumbling in the six palaces. A few days ago, when Princess Huanzhu held a dumpling banquet at the Shufang Studio, the whole palace suffered from diarrhea, except for Consort Chen—she said she had an upset stomach those days and didn't eat the dumplings. But I always feel... it is too coincidental."

The Empress Dowager mused: "You mean to say, she knew the dumplings were problematic?"

"I dare not assert," the Empress said. "I only find it suspicious. And after the incident, the Emperor favored Consort Chen even more, saying it was fortunate she didn't eat them, so she could take care of him."

The Empress Dowager remained silent, her fingers moving faster and faster over the prayer beads.

After a long while, she said: "I have taken note of these matters. Although you have been reflecting in seclusion, you must still manage the affairs of the six palaces. You must also come to the scripture reading tomorrow."

"Yes," the Empress replied, then hesitated and added, "Empress Dowager, what about that Xia Ziwei..."

"I will handle it myself," the Empress Dowager waved her hand. "You may return now."

After the Empress withdrew, the Empress Dowager sat alone in the Buddhist hall for a long time without speaking.

Nanny Sun walked in on tiptoe to add tea, and the Empress Dowager suddenly spoke: "Nanny Sun, in the three years I have been away from the palace, has the Emperor truly favored Consort Chen... to this extent?"

Nanny Sun said cautiously: "Replying to the Empress Dowager, the Emperor does indeed favor Consort Chen. For these three years, the rewards to the Yongshou Palace have never ceased, and the Emperor often stays there. The concubines of the six palaces... inevitably have some complaints."

"Complaints?" The Empress Dowager sneered. "Are they complaining that the Emperor favors Consort Chen, or that they themselves are not favored?"

Nanny Sun dared not respond.

The Empress Dowager asked again: "That Xia Ziwei, have you seen her?"

"This old servant saw her once when I went to the Shufang Studio to deliver a message yesterday," Nanny Sun recalled. "She is a gentle and delicate girl, and her manners and greetings are very proper; she does not look like an ordinary palace maid."

A sharp light flashed in the Empress Dowager’s eyes: "Pass on my imperial decree: after the scripture reading tomorrow, have that Xia Ziwei come to see me."

"Yes."

In the Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao was trying on clothes.

This pale purple palace gown was made when she first entered the palace three years ago. Now, wearing it, the waist still fit perfectly—living in luxury these years, she hadn't gained any weight.

"Your Highness looks truly beautiful in this," Suxin praised. "Elegant and yet noble."

Jiang Rao spun in front of the mirror, quite satisfied.

Just as she was thinking, Qianlong arrived.

Seeing Jiang Rao in this attire, Qianlong smiled: "Rao'er, what made you think of wearing this today? I remember this was made when you first entered the palace."

"Your Majesty still remembers?" Jiang Rao was somewhat surprised.

"Naturally, I remember." Qianlong walked to her side. "That day you were chasing butterflies in the Imperial Garden wearing this dress. I saw you from afar and thought I had seen a fairy."

Jiang Rao blushed at his words and chided: "Your Majesty is teasing me again."

"I speak the truth." Qianlong held her hand. "In these few years, you haven't changed at all; you are still just as beautiful."

Jiang Rao leaned on his shoulder: "Your Majesty only knows how to coax me into happiness. The Empress Dowager even called me frivolous yesterday."

"The Empress Dowager was just speaking casually," Qianlong comforted her.

In the Shufang Studio, Little Swallow was worrying.

"Should I go to the scripture reading tomorrow?" she asked Ziwei with a bitter face.

Ziwei said softly: "The Empress Dowager didn't summon the Princess, so there's no need for you to go."

"But Consort Ling said that when the Empress Dowager listens to scriptures, all the concubines of the six palaces must be present," Little Swallow said. "I am a princess; does that count as a concubine?"

As they were speaking, Mingyue came in to report: "Princess, Nanny Sun from the Cining Palace is here."

Little Swallow was startled: "Looking for me again?"

Nanny Sun walked in, performed a formal salute, and looked at Ziwei: "Imperial decree from the Empress Dowager: invite Miss Xia to the Cining Palace after the scripture reading tomorrow."

Ziwei’s face turned pale: "The Empress Dowager... wants to see this servant?"

"Yes," Nanny Sun said. "The Empress Dowager has heard that Miss Xia is exceptionally talented and wishes to see her."

Ziwei’s heart pounded wildly, and she instinctively looked at Little Swallow. Little Swallow was also panicked: "Nanny Sun, Ziwei is just a palace maid; why does the Empress Dowager want to see her?"

After Nanny Sun left, Ziwei’s face was as pale as paper. Little Swallow held her hand: "Ziwei, don't be afraid, I'll go with you tomorrow!"

"Princess, the Empress Dowager only summoned me alone," Ziwei shook her head. "It wouldn't be appropriate for you to go."

"Then what should we do?" Little Swallow paced anxiously. "The Empress Dowager suddenly wants to see you; it can't be anything good! Did the Empress say something?"

Ziwei: "Little Swallow, you are making too much of a fuss, it will be fine."

That night, many people did not sleep well.

Jiang Rao was thinking about how to deal with the Empress Dowager tomorrow, Ziwei was worried about the summons, Little Swallow was worried about Ziwei, and the Empress was calculating how to use the Empress Dowager’s hand to regain control of the six palaces.

chapters.title: I Have No Face to See Anyone
chapters.content:
The next morning, the Buddhist hall of the Cining Palace was filled with sandalwood incense.

The Empress Dowager sat in the main seat, and the concubines of the six palaces sat in order. Jiang Rao, wearing that pale purple palace gown, sat below Consort Ling, eyes lowered in a submissive manner, but her heart was crystal clear—on this occasion, the Empress Dowager would surely find someone to make an example of.

The chanting stopped, and the Empress Dowager indeed began to test them on Buddhist philosophy. Jiang Rao secretly rejoiced that she had prepared in advance; having flipped through a few Buddhist scriptures in her spare time over the years, although not an expert, she knew enough to handle a few polite responses.

"Consort Chen," the Empress Dowager’s voice suddenly rang out. "Tell me, how do you interpret 'Form is emptiness, emptiness is form'?"

Jiang Rao’s heart skipped a beat, but she stood up respectfully: "Replying to the Empress Dowager, in my humble opinion, this sentence means that all things in the world have no inherent nature and arise from the combination of causes and conditions. To be attached to appearances is to be caught in 'form'; to see through the illusion is to attain the nature of 'emptiness'."

Her answer was standard, neither brilliant nor wrong. The Empress Dowager stared at her for a moment and said slowly: "Since you know 'not to be attached to form,' do you know that this dress is too eye-catching?"

Here it comes. Jiang Rao sneered inwardly, but her face showed panic: "This concubine knows she is wrong..."

"Where is the wrong?"

"The wrong is in..." Jiang Rao bit her lip, "The wrong is in not knowing how to be restrained."

The Empress Dowager said indifferently, "You have been in the palace for three years, and I am aware that the Emperor favors you. However, within the six palaces, one must know their place. Today, while attending the scripture reading, although your attire is plain, look at the fabric of this dress and these Eastern pearl hairpins—which of these is not the latest tribute from this year? I have been away from the palace for only a few years, and has the atmosphere already become this extravagant?"

Silence fell over the Buddha hall. The concubines all lowered their heads, each harboring her own thoughts—the Empress Dowager was clearly using Consort Chen as an example to warn the others.

Jiang Rao knelt to plead guilty, but she was clear-headed: the Empress Dowager was using this as a pretext to curb the situation of her being the sole favorite. That was fine; being reprimanded in public today was a good excuse to keep a low profile for a while.

After the scripture reading ended, the concubines withdrew one by one.

As Jiang Rao walked out of the Cining Palace, she caught a glimpse of Ziwei waiting under the corridor. She understood immediately—the Empress Dowager was indeed going to see Ziwei alone. In the original story, it was from Ziwei’s reaction during this encounter that the Empress Dowager grew suspicious.

"Your Ladyship," Suxin whispered, "let us return to the palace."

"No rush," Jiang Rao said leisurely. "The crabapple blossoms in the Imperial Garden are in full bloom; let’s go for a stroll."

She deliberately chose a path that overlooked the corridor of the Cining Palace and, sure enough, saw Ziwei being led inside by Nanny Sun. Xiaoyanzi was hiding behind a rockery, peeking and stomping her feet in anxiety.

Jiang Rao sighed inwardly. Ziwei was truly pitiful; despite being a golden branch and jade leaf, she had to live here in constant fear. But then again... this was the plot...

Inside the Buddha hall, Ziwei knelt before the Empress Dowager.

The Empress Dowager asked her to lift her head, carefully scrutinizing that delicate face. Indeed... there were traces of Xia Yuhe from those years.

"I hear you often play chess with the Emperor?" the Empress Dowager asked slowly.

Ziwei’s voice trembled: "This servant... only serves..."

"Serves?" The Empress Dowager interrupted her. "How is it that I hear the Emperor praises your chess skills and your poetry? A palace maid with such talent?"

Ziwei’s face turned pale.

The Empress Dowager fingered her prayer beads and suddenly asked, "Since you are from Jinan, have you ever heard of Xia Yuhe?"

These words struck like a thunderbolt. Ziwei shuddered, nearly collapsing to the floor. She opened her mouth, but no sound came out.

The Empress Dowager took in her reaction, her suspicions deepening. If she were just an ordinary palace maid, why would she be so distraught at the mention of Xia Yuhe’s name?

"What? You haven't heard of her?" The Empress Dowager pressed on.

"This servant... this servant..." Ziwei’s mind went blank. After a long while, she managed to squeeze out a few words: "This servant was young at the time... and did not pay attention..."

The Empress Dowager stared at her for a long time, so long that Ziwei nearly fainted.

"Enough," the Empress Dowager waved her hand. "Since you are in the service of the Huanzhu Princess, you must serve her well. You may withdraw."

Ziwei practically crawled out of the Buddha hall. When Xiaoyanzi rushed over to support her, her body was ice-cold, and cold sweat had soaked through her clothes.

"Ziwei! What did the Empress Dowager say?" Xiaoyanzi asked anxiously.

Ziwei shook her head, tears sliding down silently. The Empress Dowager’s eyes... they were too terrifying, as if they could see through everything.

In the Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao was removing her makeup.

As Suxin helped her take off her hairpins and jewelry, she said cautiously, "Your Ladyship was wronged today."

"Wronged?" Jiang Rao looked into the mirror and removed her earrings unhurriedly. "The Empress Dowager wants to establish her authority; she has to find someone to make an example of. I am the most prominent, so naturally, I am the first to bear the brunt."

"But the Empress Dowager’s words were too harsh..."

"Harsh?" Jiang Rao smiled. "Just wait and see, there will be harsher ones to come. The Empress Dowager’s return has two purposes: first, to rectify the atmosphere of the six palaces, and second, to investigate the background of the Huanzhu Princess. She has done both today."

Suxin was puzzled: "Investigate the Huanzhu Princess’s background?"

Jiang Rao gave her a meaningful look: "Why do you think the Empress Dowager summoned Xia Ziwei alone? And specifically asked about Xia Yuhe?"

Suxin suddenly realized: "Your Ladyship means..."

"I said nothing," Jiang Rao interrupted her. "The less you know about affairs in this palace, the better."

Just as they were speaking, the Qianlong Emperor arrived.

Jiang Rao immediately put on a look of grievance, threw herself into his arms, and wept: "Your Majesty! The Empress Dowager reprimanded me in public today, saying I am extravagant, saying I am ostentatious... I have no face to see anyone anymore!"

Qianlong held her and coaxed: "The Empress Mother was just speaking her mind, don't take it to heart."

"How can I not take it to heart?" Jiang Rao raised her teary eyes. "All the concubines of the six palaces heard it; they will surely mock me from now on... I cannot go on living!"

Qianlong had a headache from her crying and had no choice but to say: "Alright, alright, I will go speak to the Empress Mother tomorrow and ask her not to make things difficult for you in the future."

"Really?" Jiang Rao sobbed.

"Really."

Only then did Jiang Rao break into a smile, leaning into his arms and acting spoiled. But in her heart, she thought: The things the Empress Dowager wants to investigate will be uncovered sooner or later. When that time comes, this palace will truly become lively.

Inside the Cining Palace, the Empress Dowager was listening to Nanny Sun’s report.

"When Miss Xia left, her face was deathly pale, and she could barely walk steadily," Nanny Sun whispered. "The Huanzhu Princess was waiting outside, looking extremely anxious."

The Empress Dowager fingered her prayer beads and said slowly, "This Xia Ziwei... her reaction was too abnormal. If she truly is Xia Yuhe’s daughter..."

She did not continue, but Nanny Sun already understood: "Empress Dowager, should this old servant send someone to Jinan..."

"Yes," the Empress Dowager said firmly. "Send someone to investigate quietly: how many children did Xia Yuhe have, were they boys or girls, and where are they now? Remember, investigate in secret; do not alert anyone."

"Yes."

The Empress Dowager looked out the window. Twilight was closing in, and the lights of the Forbidden City were being lit one by one.

In the Shufang Studio, Ziwei did not sleep all night.

She sat by the window, looking at the full moon in the sky, remembering her mother’s dying wish: "Ziwei, you must find your father... let him know that your mother waited for him her whole life..."

Tears fell silently.

Xiaoyanzi walked in quietly and hugged her from behind: "Ziwei, don't be afraid. With me here, no one can bully you."

Ziwei turned and hugged Xiaoyanzi, sobbing uncontrollably.

"Xiaoyanzi," she choked out, "if... if one day, the truth is revealed, will you blame me?"

"Blame you for what?" Xiaoyanzi was confused.

"Blame me for not telling you sooner... blame me for dragging you into this..."

"What foolish things are you saying!" Xiaoyanzi said anxiously. "We are sworn sisters; we share joys and sorrows together! No matter what your identity is, you are my good sister!"

Ziwei held her tightly, tears streaming down her face.

Outside the window, the night was deep.

Meanwhile, in the Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao was leaning in Qianlong’s arms, calculating the upcoming plot.

Next should be the cuju (football) match, and then the incognito tour. Thinking about the incognito tour made her excited.

With this thought, she found a comfortable position in Qianlong’s arms and fell into a deep sleep.

chapters.title: The Cuju Disturbance in the Imperial Garden
chapters.content:
Five days after the Empress Dowager’s scripture reading, the weather was fine.

The Empress Dowager was strolling in the Imperial Garden accompanied by Nanny Sun, thinking about the recent events in the palace and still preoccupied with Xia Ziwei’s abnormal behavior that day. Just as they reached the lawn on the east side, they suddenly heard bursts of laughter.

"What is that sound?" The Empress Dowager frowned.

Nanny Sun walked a few steps ahead to look, and when she returned, her expression was troubled: "Replying to the Empress Dowager, it is... it is the Huanzhu Princess, the Fifth Prince, and Guard Fu playing cuju."

The Empress Dowager’s face darkened.

Ziwei also knelt down: "Empress Dowager, please calm your anger, it is this servant..."

"You are also guilty!" The Empress Dowager pointed at Ziwei. "Following your master in such nonsense all day long! Give her twenty slaps!"

"Imperial Grandmother, no!" Xiaoyanzi was so anxious that tears came out. "I was the one who wanted to play; just punish me!"

As they were arguing, Qianlong’s voice came from afar: "What is going on here?"

Qianlong was seen walking over with Jiang Rao. Jiang Rao was wearing a pale pink casual dress today, adorned with a simple pearl flower, looking much plainer than she had that day.

Qianlong walked up to them, saw the people kneeling on the ground, and looked at the cuju ball on the ground. He understood most of it: "Imperial Mother, please calm your anger. Has Xiaoyanzi angered you again?"

The Empress Dowager pointed at Xiaoyanzi: "Your Majesty, see for yourself! This good daughter of yours, playing with a ball in the Imperial Garden—what kind of decorum is this!"

Qianlong glanced at the cuju ball and said gently, "Imperial Mother, cuju is originally a way to strengthen the body. Xiaoyanzi is lively and active; it is common for her to kick a ball around."

"Common?" The Empress Dowager sneered. "Making noise and playing in the Imperial Garden—what kind of decorum is this!"

Xiaoyanzi suddenly lifted her head. Tears were still hanging on her face, but her eyes were bright: "Imperial Father! Since Imperial Grandmother says playing ball is bad, let’s hold a proper competition! Right here! Let’s hold a 'Vent-Your-Frustrations Ball Tournament,' let all the concubines come to watch, and kick away all our unhappiness!"

Qianlong was stunned: "Vent-Your-Frustrations Ball Tournament?"

"Yes!" Xiaoyanzi became more enthusiastic as she spoke. "We will organize teams for a competition, make it official! You can be the referee, Imperial Father, and let everyone see that cuju is a proper activity!"

Yongqi also said, "Imperial Father, this is a good idea. The palace hasn't been this lively for a long time."

Qianlong was moved and looked at the Empress Dowager: "Imperial Mother, what do you think..."

The Empress Dowager looked at Xiaoyanzi’s expectant eyes, then at Qianlong, and finally flicked her sleeves and left: "Enough! If you father and son want to spoil her, I have nothing to say!"

Watching the Empress Dowager’s departing back, Xiaoyanzi broke into a smile through her tears: "Thank you, Imperial Father!"

Qianlong glared at her: "You girl, you only know how to cause trouble for me. But this 'Vent-Your-Frustrations Ball Tournament'... it is quite interesting. How do you want to compete?"

Xiaoyanzi’s eyes lit up: "We will divide into two teams! One team called the 'Prince Team,' and one team called the 'Princess Team'! I will be the captain of the Princess Team!"

"Nonsense," Qianlong laughed. "A girl like you, what kind of captain would you be."

"I want to be!" Xiaoyanzi tugged on Qianlong’s sleeve and acted spoiled. "You promised, Imperial Father! You cannot go back on your word!"

Qianlong had no choice but to give in: "Fine, fine, fine, everything as you wish. But..." he paused, "for this Princess Team, where will you find people?"

Xiaoyanzi’s eyes rolled: "Ziwei can! Mingyue and Caixia can too! And... and..."

Erkang suddenly spoke up: "If the Princess is short of people, I know a girl who is quite skilled; we could invite her to help."

"Who?" Xiaoyanzi asked curiously.

"She is a friend of mine from outside the palace, named Liu Hong," Erkang said. "She has practiced martial arts since she was a child and plays cuju very well."

Qianlong pondered for a moment: "A person from outside the palace entering the palace... I fear it is not according to the rules."

"Imperial Father—" Xiaoyanzi dragged out her voice, "it’s just one person! Our competition needs to be lively; it won't be fun if there aren't enough people!"

Qianlong, pestered by her until he had a headache, waved his hand: "Enough, enough. Let Erkang make the arrangements. But this is the only time; do not let it become a precedent."

"Thank you, Imperial Father!" Xiaoyanzi jumped for joy.

On the way back to Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao walked at a leisurely pace.

Suxin whispered, "Your Ladyship, this Princess Huanzhu is truly a handful."

Jiang Rao chuckled, "Isn't that good? The palace hasn't been this lively in a long time."

She remembered that in the original story, this cuju match was quite spectacular. The "Princess Team" assembled by Xiaoyanzi played against the "Prince Team" led by Yongqi, and the arrival of the siblings Liu Qing and Liu Hong to help out caused quite a few funny incidents. And after this match, it would be time for the incognito tour.

"Your Ladyship seems to be looking forward to it?" Suxin asked.

"Naturally," Jiang Rao said. "How could I miss such an interesting event?"

That evening, when Qianlong came to Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao leaned into his arms and said, "Your Majesty, I would also like to watch the cuju match."

Qianlong laughed, "You should go, of course. But..." He pinched Jiang Rao's cheek, "You are not allowed to act as recklessly as Xiaoyanzi."

"I wouldn't dream of it," Jiang Rao said coquettishly. "I will just watch the match quietly."

In Shufang Studio, Xiaoyanzi was excitedly planning the match.

"Ziwei, you must participate! Mingyue and Caixia will join too! Liu Hong is coming as well, but we are still short a few people..." Xiaoyanzi counted on her fingers.

Ziwei said helplessly, "Xiaoyanzi, I don't know how to play..."

"I'll teach you!" Xiaoyanzi patted her chest. "It's very simple!"

Just as they were talking, Erkang arrived, followed by a young woman dressed in green martial attire. The girl was about seventeen or eighteen, with delicate features and a hint of heroic spirit in her every movement.

"Xiaoyanzi, look who's here," Erkang said.

Xiaoyanzi's eyes lit up. "Ahhh, Liu Hong! Erkang, you really brought her into the palace! This is wonderful!"

"It's perfect!" Xiaoyanzi grabbed Liu Hong's hand. "With you joining us, our Princess Team will definitely win!"

The match was set for three days later. As the news spread, all six palaces began to look forward to it.

Xiaoyanzi was busy running around, both training the "Princess Team" and preparing for the match. Ziwei stayed by her side to help.

In Cining Palace, the Empress Dowager was listening to Mother Sun's report.

"Princess Huanzhu is indeed preparing for a cuju match, and she has even brought people in from outside the palace," Mother Sun said. "His Majesty has also approved it."

The Empress Dowager twirled her prayer beads and said indifferently, "Let her make a scene. Once the match is over, I will settle the score with her."

She paused. "Is there any news... from Jinan?"

"Not yet," Mother Sun whispered. "But it should be soon."

The Empress Dowager looked out the window; the sound of Xiaoyanzi's laughter could be faintly heard from the direction of the Imperial Garden. That girl... if she really wasn't Xia Yuhe's daughter, then Xia Ziwei...

A sharp glint flashed in her eyes.

In Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao was trying on clothes.

"Your Ladyship, is this outfit too plain?" Suxin held up a moon-white dress embroidered with plum blossoms.

"Plain is better," Jiang Rao said. "The Empress Dowager just scolded me for being extravagant a few days ago; I dare not be flashy again."

She adjusted her hair in the mirror, but her mind was on the match three days later. In the original story, this cuju match was full of climaxes, and Xiaoyanzi and the others even prepared a special surprise for Qianlong.

chapters.title: The Storm Before the Cuju Match
chapters.content:
Two days before the cuju match, the atmosphere in Shufang Studio was tense.

Xiaoyanzi counted the "Princess Team" members with a worried face: "Ziwei, Mingyue, Caixia, Liu Hong, and the few palace maids sent by Consort Ling—we are still short three people!"

The palace maids who had originally agreed to participate had all claimed to be ill early that morning. After Ziwei inquired, she found out that Mother Rong had privately "warned" them—anyone who dared to join Princess Huanzhu's cuju team would have a hard time in the palace from then on.

"That Mother Rong!" Xiaoyanzi stomped her feet in anger. "His Imperial Father told her to reflect behind closed doors, yet she's still causing trouble in secret!"

Ziwei said softly, "Princess, getting angry now won't help. We must find people quickly, or the match will be a disaster."

Xiaoyanzi bit her lip and paced around the room. Suddenly, her eyes lit up: "I have it! I'll go ask Consort Chen!"

Ziwei was stunned: "Consort Chen? She holds the rank of Consort; how can she come to play ball?"

"Why not?" Xiaoyanzi said righteously. "She's not that old, and besides..." She lowered her voice, "I heard she knew some martial arts before she entered the palace!"

In Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao was looking at new fabric sent by the Imperial Household Department.

Suxin was tidying up nearby when she heard an announcement from outside: "Princess Huanzhu has arrived—"

Jiang Rao raised an eyebrow: "Why is she here?"

Xiaoyanzi walked in with Ziwei, her face full of smiles: "Greetings to Consort Chen!"

Jiang Rao put down the fabric and gave a half-smile: "What brings Princess Huanzhu here today? Aren't you busy preparing for the cuju match?"

Xiaoyanzi rubbed her hands together, showing a rare moment of bashfulness: "Well... Your Ladyship, I've come to ask for your help..."

"Oh?" Jiang Rao signaled Suxin to serve tea. "If the Princess has something to say, just say it."

Xiaoyanzi leaned in closer and whispered: "Our 'Princess Team' is short of people... The Empress is causing trouble and scared off the maids who promised to join. Now we don't have enough players... I want to invite you to join us!"

"Pfft—" Jiang Rao nearly spat out her tea. "What did you say?"

Ziwei quickly said, "Your Ladyship, please forgive us, the Princess is just anxious..."

"I'm not anxious!" Xiaoyanzi said urgently. "Your Ladyship, look at how young you are, your skills must be great! Please help us! We can't let the 'Prince Team' look down on us!"

Jiang Rao set down her teacup, feeling a bit tempted. She had been in the palace for three years; while her life was wealthy, it was also boring. Playing cuju... it sounded quite interesting.

But on the surface, she remained composed: "Princess, you jest. I am a Consort; how can I go play ball? It would be improper."

"How is it improper?" Xiaoyanzi was anxious. "His Imperial Father approved the match! Your Ladyship, please help! I promise, you just need to stand in a position on the field; you don't even have to actually kick!"

Jiang Rao was still hesitating when an announcement came from outside: "His Majesty has arrived—"

Qianlong walked in and, seeing Xiaoyanzi, laughed: "You girl, what are you doing here?"

Xiaoyanzi quickly said, "Imperial Father, I am asking Consort Chen to join the cuju match! Our team is short of players!"

Qianlong was stunned, then his face darkened: "Nonsense! Consort Chen holds the rank of Consort; how can she go play ball?"

"Why not?" Xiaoyanzi tugged on Qianlong's sleeve. "Imperial Father, didn't you say cuju is a proper activity? If the Consort participates, it's just sharing the fun with the people!"

Qianlong looked at Jiang Rao: "Rao'er, you must not follow her in this nonsense."

Jiang Rao lowered her eyes: "His Majesty is right. I... am indeed not suited for it."

But the urge to try it out wouldn't go away.

Seeing that she couldn't be persuaded, Xiaoyanzi left, dejected.

After Xiaoyanzi left, Jiang Rao said softly to Qianlong: "Your Majesty, actually... I really do want to try."

Qianlong frowned: "Rao'er, you are a consort. Playing ball in front of so many people, what would that look like? Besides, playing ball is a strenuous activity, and your health is not suited for it."

"But I feel stifled in the palace..." Jiang Rao leaned on his shoulder. "Your Majesty, look, Princess Huanzhu can play, why can't I? I won't do anything dangerous, just standing on the field would be enough..."

Qianlong looked at her expectant eyes, his resolve wavering. It was true that keeping her confined in the palace for the past few years had stifled her.

"Fine," Qianlong sighed. "If you really want to go... I approve. But there are a few conditions."

Jiang Rao's eyes lit up: "Your Majesty, tell me!"

"First, no dangerous moves. Second, dress modestly; don't run around wildly like Xiaoyanzi. Third..." Qianlong tapped her nose, "If you get tired, come off the field; don't force yourself."

"I obey your decree!" Jiang Rao beamed.

In Shufang Studio, Xiaoyanzi was worrying when Yongqi rushed over.

"Xiaoyanzi, I heard you're short of people?"

"Fifth Prince!" Xiaoyanzi's eyes lit up. "Do you have a way?"

Yongqi laughed: "I found two young maids from the Prince's quarters who are willing to participate. Plus, Consort Chen..."

"Consort Chen agreed?" Xiaoyanzi asked in surprise.

"His Imperial Father approved," Yongqi said. "But you must take good care of her and don't let her get tired."

"Don't worry!" Xiaoyanzi patted her chest. "I will treat her like a Bodhisattva!"

*In the Palace of Earthly Tranquility, the Empress heard Mother Rong's report and sneered: "Consort Chen is joining too? Good, then let her go and make a fool of herself."

Mother Rong whispered: "Your Ladyship, should we..."

"No need," the Empress waved her hand. "If Consort Chen wants to lose face, we'll just watch. The Emperor has pampered her for several years; it's time for the Empress Dowager to see what kind of character she has."
