The day before the match, Jiang Rao tried on her altered riding outfit in Yongshou Palace.

It was a lotus-root-colored short outfit; the fabric was light, and the cuffs and trouser legs were cinched, making it convenient for movement without losing decorum.

Suxin helped her adjust it, worried: "Your Ladyship, are you really going to play? What if..."

"What if what?" Jiang Rao spun around in the mirror. "Don't worry, I know my limits."

She did know her limits—as a transmigrator, she knew Xiaoyanzi would shine in this match, and all she had to do was perform appropriately on the field, neither stealing the spotlight too much nor appearing too useless.

Most importantly... she really wanted to have some fun.

In Cining Palace, the Empress Dowager also heard the news.

"Consort Chen is participating in the cuju match?" The Empress Dowager twirled her prayer beads. "She certainly knows how to join in the fun."

Mother Sun said: "Empress Dowager, should this old servant go..."

"No need," the Empress Dowager said indifferently. "Let her go. I want to see what kind of tricks she can pull."

On the day of the match, the east lawn of the Imperial Garden was bustling with activity.

The stands had been set up long ago, and the consorts from various palaces arrived one after another. The Empress sat in the main seat accompanying the Empress Dowager, and Consort Ling, Consort Qing, and others were also present.

On the sidelines, the "Princess Team" and the "Prince Team" were warming up.

When Xiaoyanzi saw Jiang Rao arrive, she ran over excitedly: "Consort Chen! You really came!"

Jiang Rao was indeed dressed neatly today; the lotus-root-colored riding outfit accentuated her upright posture, and her hair was simply tied up with a white jade hairpin, looking fresh and elegant.

"Since I promised, I naturally wouldn't break my word," Jiang Rao laughed. "But the Princess will have to look after me, as I don't know how to play."

"Your Ladyship, don't worry!" Little Swallow patted her chest. "Just stand on the field; when the ball comes, just pass it to me!"

On the other side, the "Prince Team" was led by Yongqi, with Erkang and Ertai in the ranks, along with several guards skilled in wrestling.

Qianlong had also arrived. Seeing Jiang Rao in this attire, a flash of astonishment crossed his eyes, but he immediately frowned: "Rao'er, do you really have to go on the field?"

"The Emperor has already given his permission; you can't go back on your word now." Jiang Rao revealed a rare, mischievous smile.

Qianlong shook his head helplessly and took his seat in the main position.

The match was about to begin.

Little Swallow grabbed Jiang Rao's hand: "Your Ladyship, don't be nervous, just follow my lead!"

Jiang Rao nodded, though she felt a bit excited inside. In the three years since she had transmigrated, she had never been this "unrestrained."

As the referee gave the order, the match officially began.

chapters.title: A Good Show Begins, Surprise!
chapters.content:
On the east lawn of the Imperial Garden, the atmosphere had reached its peak.

The two teams stood on opposite sides. For the Princess Team, Little Swallow took the lead, followed closely by Ziwei. Jiang Rao was positioned slightly further back, flanked by Mingyue and Caixia. Liu Hong and several palace maids who knew some martial arts stood guard around Jiang Rao—this was per Qianlong's specific instructions to ensure the safety of Consort Chen.

Opposite them, the Prince Team was led by Yongqi, Erkang, and Ertai, with several guards from the Imperial Wrestling Camp rubbing their hands in anticipation. Yongqi looked at Little Swallow with eyes full of smiles, then nodded slightly toward Jiang Rao as a greeting.

A gong sounded, and the match began!

Little Swallow charged out like a wild horse off its tether. Yongqi, prepared, moved to block her path. The two began to scramble for the ball, their movements so fast they were dazzling.

Jiang Rao stood in her position, following Little Swallow's prior instructions, moving her feet only slightly while keeping her eyes locked on the bouncing ball. The cheers and applause from the sidelines surged like waves. She took a deep breath, feeling a sense of excitement she hadn't experienced since her days on the school sports field.

"Your Ladyship, the ball is coming!" Liu Hong suddenly shouted.

It turned out that Little Swallow had made a feint, managed to steal the ball from under Yongqi's feet, and sent a long pass. The ball flew straight toward Jiang Rao, perfectly aimed. Everyone on and off the field was stunned—no one had expected Little Swallow to actually pass the ball to Consort Chen.

Jiang Rao was also startled, but her body reacted faster than her brain, and she instinctively lifted her foot to receive it. The ball hit her instep with a "thud," causing a slight sting, but it stopped steadily.

"Good!" someone shouted.

Jiang Rao didn't have time to think. Seeing Little Swallow charging forward, she mimicked the *cuju* moves from her memory, lightly flicking the ball with her instep toward Little Swallow. Though not professional, it was quite a decent attempt.

"Great pass, Your Ladyship!" Little Swallow cheered, caught the ball, and turned, only to have her path blocked by Erkang.

On the viewing stand, Qianlong had been gripping the armrests nervously, but seeing Jiang Rao's skillful reception and pass, he finally relaxed, a hint of a smile appearing in his eyes. The Empress sat beside the Empress Dowager, watching coldly, her handkerchief tightly clenched in her hand.

The match continued. Little Swallow truly gave it her all; at one point, she dove to save the ball and fell heavily to the ground, causing Yongqi's face to change with concern. Jiang Rao watched clearly from the field, sighing inwardly at the deep affection between these two bickering lovers.

When it was the Prince Team's turn to attack, Erkang launched a powerful shot. The ball flew straight toward the back of the Princess Team—exactly where Jiang Rao was standing. Jiang Rao instinctively tried to dodge, but heard Ziwei cry out: "Your Ladyship, watch out!" Ziwei then dove over, using her body to block the ball.

"Ziwei!" Little Swallow rushed over to help her up.

Jiang Rao hurried to crouch down: "Ziwei, are you alright?"

Ziwei shook her head, though her face was pale. The impact had been quite hard.

On the sidelines, seeing Ziwei injured, Erkang lost his composure, and his subsequent defense had several openings. Little Swallow seized the opportunity, bypassed two people, and made a beautiful final shot—

The ball hit the net!

"It's in! It's in!" The Princess Team cheered.

The gong signaling the end of the match sounded; the Princess Team had actually beaten the Prince Team. Little Swallow hugged Ziwei, laughing and jumping, while Yongqi, Erkang, and the others shook their heads with smiles and came forward to offer congratulations.

Jiang Rao stood in the crowd, breathing slightly hard, her cheeks flushed from the exercise. She raised a hand to wipe the fine sweat from her forehead, and as she turned, she met Qianlong's smiling gaze. She pursed her lips and smiled, a long-lost sense of exhilaration welling up inside her.

After the match, everyone moved to the viewing stand.

Little Swallow suddenly bowed to Qianlong with a mysterious air: "Imperial Father, the match is over, but we have another 'surprise' to present to you!"

Qianlong laughed: "Oh? What other tricks do you have?"

Little Swallow clapped her hands. More than twenty palace maids appeared, dressed in red, green, yellow, and blue, each holding a long colorful silk ribbon, running toward the field from all directions. They moved with light, well-trained steps and took their positions in the center of the field.

Music began to play softly, and the maids danced to the rhythm. The silk ribbons flew in the air, sometimes like a rainbow piercing the sun, sometimes like drifting clouds. Just as the crowd was dazzled, the maids suddenly gathered and then dispersed—

The ribbons were pulled taut, forming a giant character for "Longevity" (Shou) in the center of the field!

The "Shou" character had a red silk base with gold-threaded edges, shining brilliantly under the sun. The maids knelt and shouted in unison: "Wishing the Emperor a long and prosperous life!"

The entire arena was silent for a moment, then erupted in exclamations of wonder.

Qianlong was stunned. He looked at the giant "Shou" character made of silk, then at the sincere faces of the maids, and finally his gaze landed on Little Swallow and the others. These children must have put so much thought and training into this surprise for him.

The Empress Dowager was also moved. She nodded slowly and said softly: "I finally understand why the Emperor likes Little Swallow so much."

Consort Ling said gently: "Empress Dowager, although Princess Huanzhu is mischievous, her filial piety is sincere. Look at this performance she arranged; it is lively yet solemn—she truly put her heart into it."

Qianlong stood up, tears glistening in his eyes. He walked down from the stand to the field and personally helped Little Swallow and Yongqi, who were still kneeling, to their feet.

"Good children, your intentions, Imperial Father has received them." He added, "This is the most special birthday gift I have ever seen."

Little Swallow's eyes sparkled: "Does Imperial Father like it?"

"I like it, I like it very much." Qianlong looked at the giant "Shou" character. "This gift is more precious than any gold, silver, or jewelry."

Ziwei said warmly: "Your Majesty, these palace maids trained for ten full days. Little Swallow supervised them personally every day, not allowing a single mistake."

Qianlong patted Little Swallow's shoulder and turned to the crowd: "Today's *cuju* match was well-organized, and this birthday gift is even better! Seeing you brothers and sisters in harmony and the monarch and subjects of one mind—this is the true spirit of our Great Qing!"

Everyone shouted "Long live" in unison. Little Swallow smiled brightly, Ziwei's eyes filled with tears, and Yongqi, Erkang, and the others also wore smiles.

Jiang Rao stood among the concubines, looking at the giant silk "Shou" character, her heart filled with emotion. This was the most classic scene from *My Fair Princess*; no matter how many times she saw it, it was moving.

That night, Yongshou Palace.

Jiang Rao had just finished bathing and changed into a moon-white silk nightgown. Her long hair was loosely pinned up, and she was leaning on a couch, letting Suxin massage her legs.

"Is Your Ladyship tired today?" Suxin asked with a gentle touch. "I saw you running around quite a bit on the field."

"My legs are a bit sore," Jiang Rao said, closing her eyes. "But it felt great."

Just as she was speaking, an announcement came from outside: "The Emperor has arrived!"

Jiang Rao hurried to rise, but Qianlong had already strode in, waving his hand to excuse her from the formalities: "Stay seated. You're exhausted today, no need for ceremony."

He sat beside her and naturally took over Suxin's work, massaging her legs himself. Suxin tactfully withdrew.

"Your Majesty..." Jiang Rao felt a bit embarrassed.

"Don't move." Qianlong's technique was actually quite good. "On the field today, I saw you receive that ball; it was quite impressive."

Jiang Rao pursed her lips and smiled: "That was just a blind cat stumbling upon a dead mouse." She tilted her head to look at him: "Is the Emperor still angry at me for being so reckless?"

"Angry? Of course I'm angry." Qianlong deliberately put on a stern face. "A consort, running and jumping in front of so many people—what kind of decorum is that?"

Jiang Rao leaned closer, her voice soft: "Then punish me, Your Majesty."

Qianlong was amused by her expression and pinched her nose: "Punish you with what? Punish you by making you play another match for me tomorrow?"

"That won't do." Jiang Rao leaned into his arms: "My legs are still sore... Your Majesty, you don't know, it really hurts when the ball hits your feet."

Qianlong held her and said gently: "You're the one to blame, insisting on playing when you don't even know how. What if you had gotten hurt?"

"Isn't the Emperor here to protect me?" Jiang Rao said in a sweet, soft voice. "Besides, I've been stifled in the palace for so long; it was a rare opportunity to stretch my limbs... Your Majesty, you don't know, hearing everyone cheer today and seeing Little Swallow and the others so full of spirit, I felt like I had become several years younger myself."

Hearing this, Qianlong felt his heart soften. It was true; she had been in the palace for three years, always acting as the proper Consort Chen, and he had almost forgotten that she was just a girl in her early twenties.

"Very well, as long as you are happy." He sighed softly. "But in the future, if you want to exercise, just play in the courtyard of Yongshou Palace; there's no need to go out in public."

Jiang Rao rubbed against his chest: "I understand."

The two embraced quietly for a moment, and Jiang Rao suddenly remembered something and looked up: "Oh, right, Your Majesty, I also have a gift for you."

"Oh?" Qianlong raised an eyebrow. "Didn't I already receive a gift today?"

"That was Little Swallow and the others' intention; this is mine." Jiang Rao took a brocade box from the small drawer by the couch and handed it to Qianlong.

Qianlong opened it, and inside was a pair of glass paperweights. The glass was crystal clear, with fine gold foil swirling inside, shining brilliantly in the candlelight. Even more wonderful was the tiny inscription at the bottom of the paperweights; looking closely, it was a couplet:

*The four seas are at peace, bearing the purple aura,**The prosperous age of the nine provinces is bathed in the spring breeze.*

The handwriting was elegant and neat, clearly written by Jiang Rao herself.

"I made these a few days ago," Jiang Rao said softly. "The glass was scrap material I asked the Imperial Household Department to find, and the gold foil was melted down from old jewelry... I carved the characters myself; I ruined three pairs before I finally succeeded with this one."

Qianlong stroked the paperweights; they felt warm and smooth to the touch. As the Son of Heaven, he had seen every rare treasure imaginable, but this small pair of paperweights, made by her own hands, was more precious than any tribute.

"What made you think of making this?" his voice was gentle.

Jiang Rao leaned against his shoulder, her sleepiness gradually taking hold, and her voice became slurred: "The paperweight you use when reviewing memorials is getting old... These bright ones might be easier on your eyes, Your Majesty... And 'Peace Throughout the Four Seas,' 'Prosperity Across the Nine Provinces'—these are my wishes for you..."

As her voice trailed off, she had already fallen into a deep sleep.

Qianlong sat by the side of the couch, watching her for a long time. In the candlelight, her sleeping face was serene and beautiful, her eyelashes casting soft shadows beneath her eyes. He recalled how she looked on the polo field during the day—the lotus-root-colored riding habit accentuating her upright posture, the flash of surprise in her eyes when she caught the ball, and now, the slight upturn of her lips in her dreams.

He carefully placed the glass paperweight back into its brocade box, set it by her pillow, and then gently lifted her and placed her onto the bed.

The bed curtains were lowered, and moonlight filtered through the window lattice, spilling onto the pair of glass paperweights. The gold foil shimmered faintly in the darkness, as if holding the glimmer of the entire starry sky.

Qianlong lay down and pulled Jiang Rao into his arms. She leaned into him unconsciously, her breathing steady and long.

The sound of the watchman’s drum drifted from afar outside the window; the night was deep.

Yongshou Palace was tranquil, with only the moonlight flowing silently, guarding the warmth of the room.
